A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CG-MLLM research, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendix A and Figures 9-12, which were also inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and captioning results in Tables 1-2, qualitative outputs, and AdaLN and VAE reconstruction analyses in Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds user-preference scores, component ablations, resource measurements, and additional generated examples in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.5 retain the Qwen3-VL TokenAR/BlockAR architecture, frozen Hunyuan3D-2.1 VAE, masking and positional strategies, decoding, and staged training. Alternative backbones and components in v2 are ablation configurations, not changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same source datasets and already demonstrate image- and text-conditioned 3D generation and object captioning. v2 identifies toys4k within Trellis-500K as the held-out subset, without establishing changed coverage. The appendix adds examples of existing tasks; user ratings add an evaluation procedure.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 4 expand generation comparisons beyond SAR3D and ShapeLLM-Omni to Michelangelo, CraftsMan, Hunyuan3D-2.1, TRELLIS, and SAM3D. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set to non-MLLM systems. Captioning comparators in Table 2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 removes Uni3D evaluation and adds user-preference evaluation using 100 questionnaires and approximately 2,400 data points. New experiments vary VAE, MoT, backbone, and token counts; resource profiling spans 512-5120 tokens, with training measured on eight GPUs at 20,480 tokens per GPU. These are additional protocols, not replacements for the retained main training recipe.

E4.justification: New Section 4.7 and Table 3 investigate VAE capacity, MoT, backbone choice, and token-budget effects on generation quality. Tables 4-5 add training and inference resource-scaling analyses. These substantially extend the retained AdaLN, point-sampling, and failure-case analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. v2's questionnaire and response counts describe study size; its statement about statistical meaningfulness does not introduce an uncertainty estimate or test.

E6.justification: Retained automatic scores in Table 1 and all captioning scores in Table 2 are unchanged. New comparisons report TRELLIS p-FID 7.36 versus CG-MLLM's 12.55, and SAM3D user preference 3.45 versus 3.32. Tables 3-5 add ablation and resource results, and Appendix A adds qualitative outputs. The three Uni3D scores are removed.

T1.justification: The rectified-flow interpolation, velocity, loss, and inference equations in Section 2.2 remain equivalent. No formal definitions, assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added. The new scaling discussion interprets measurements rather than establishing a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly claim that learning 3D generation transfers back to perception and improves image-based 3D understanding. This adds a substantive claim while retaining the central unified captioning/generation contributions and conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly interprets the unchanged captioning comparison as generation-to-perception transfer and explicitly discusses shortcomings against non-MLLM generators. Section 4.7 adds scaling interpretations and explains decreasing training memory through smaller batches. Existing failure explanations and the main limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly identifies the held-out toys4k subset. Tables 4-5 document profiling budgets, batch and 3D-sample counts, memory, and timing. The existing implementation recipe is retained, and no code or data release information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds the SAM 3D reference and removes Uni3D alongside its metric. It also explicitly positions performance relative to non-MLLM generators. The related-work survey and distinctions from earlier MoT architectures otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. Changes include focused additions to the abstract, introduction, and discussion; a new ablation subsection, impact statement, acknowledgements, and appendix; expanded author information; and author-year citation formatting. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column ICML formatting, substantially relocating and resizing displays. Table 1 gains method groups and a different metric column, Figure 4 expands its comparisons, Tables 3-5 are added, and Appendix A introduces four galleries. Most other existing figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited validation of architectural choices and efficiency through Table 3's component comparisons and Tables 4-5's resource measurements. The non-MLLM comparisons also provide important context and expose performance gaps, while the appendix supplies additional inspectable outputs. These gains outweigh the unexplained Uni3D removal and weaknesses in the new evidence interpretation: the user study is underdescribed, and the generation-to-perception claim lacks a control isolating that effect.
